ko_meaning: 다른 사람에게 잘못해서 마음이 편하지 않다
ko_meaning_en: To feel uneasy because you did something wrong to someone

example.en: I'm really sorry I'm late.

form.q_en: Pick the correct '-아서/어서' form of 늦다 (to be late).
form.why: The vowel in 늦 is ㅡ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -어서: 늦어서 = because I'm late.

ko_meaning: 어른에게 미안한 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to tell an older person that you are sorry

example.en: I'm sorry I couldn't do my homework.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 하다.
form.why: 하다 + -여서 becomes 해서 (because I did). -아서/어서 never takes the past tense, and -러 needs 가다/오다.

en: to be thankful; to be grateful
ko_meaning: 남이 나에게 좋은 일을 해 줘서 마음이 기쁘다
ko_meaning_en: Glad in your heart because someone did something good for you

example.en: Thank you for the present.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 고맙다.
form.why: 고맙다 is ㅂ-irregular: the ㅂ changes to 우, so 고맙 + 어요 → 고마워요.

ko_meaning_en: To feel good because you meet someone

example.en: Nice to see you again.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that gives the reason (glad because we met).
form.why: -아서 links a reason to a feeling: 만나서 반가워요. -지만 means 'but', and -러/-려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람의 좋은 일을 같이 기뻐하다
ko_meaning_en: To be happy together about someone's good news

example.en: I bought a cake to celebrate my friend's birthday.

tokens.note: a noun can describe the next noun

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'in order to'.
form.why: -(으)려고 means 'in order to' and can come before any verb. -(으)러 only works before 가다/오다.

ko_meaning_en: A respectful word for father and mother

example.en: My parents live in Busan.

tokens.note: honorific -세요; the ㄹ of 살 drops

form.q_en: Pick the honorific form of 살다 for parents.
form.why: Use -(으)세요 to show respect for parents. With ㄹ-stem verbs the ㄹ drops before -세요: 살다 → 사세요.

ko_meaning_en: The man a woman is married to

example.ko: 남편은 요리를 잘하지만 청소는 안 해요.
example.roman: Nampyeoneun yorireul jalhajiman cheongsoneun an haeyo.
example.en: My husband cooks well but doesn't clean.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'but'.
form.ko: 남편은 요리를 잘하___ 청소는 안 해요.
form.why: -지만 means 'but' and links two opposite facts. -(으)려고/-(으)러 show purpose, and 하다 never takes -아서 (it becomes 해서).

ko_meaning_en: The woman a man is married to

example.en: I'm going to go to the market with my wife.

form.q_en: Pick the particle 'with' that fits after a vowel.
form.why: 와 is used after a vowel (아내), 과 after a consonant. With 같이 it means 'together with'.

ko_meaning_en: A boy born to his parents

example.en: My son can't swim yet.

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle that fits after a consonant.
form.why: 은 marks the topic after a consonant (아들); 는 is for vowels. 을 and 에 do not fit here.

ko_meaning_en: A girl born to her parents

example.en: The picture my daughter drew is pretty.

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle that fits after a consonant.
form.why: 딸 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이 (가 is for vowels). Inside a modifier clause, the subject takes 이/가.

ko_meaning_en: A person who comes to a shop or a home

example.en: There aren't many customers at the store today.

form.q_en: Pick the form that makes 'not many' with -지 않다.
form.why: -지 않다 makes a negative: 많다 → 많지 않아요 (there aren't many).

ko_meaning_en: A person who lives nearby

example.en: The neighbor next door is very kind.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 친절하다 before a noun.
form.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before a noun in the present: 친절하다 → 친절한 사람. -는 is for action verbs.

ko_meaning_en: A friendly word for calling an adult man

example.en: The taxi driver knows the roads well.

tokens.note: 택시 아저씨 = a casual word for a taxi driver

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 알다 (to know).
form.why: 알 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 알아요. (아라요 is only how it sounds.)

ko_meaning_en: A word for calling a woman of married age

example.en: The lady at the shop gave me more rice cake.

form.q_en: Pick the honorific past form of 주다 for the lady.
form.why: Add -시- for respect, then the past -었어요: 주 + 시 + 었어요 → 주셨어요.

ko_meaning: 듣는 사람들을 모두 높여 부르는 말
ko_meaning_en: A respectful word for calling all the listeners

example.en: You can all do it too.

form.q_en: Pick the form that completes 'can do' (-(으)ㄹ 수 있다).
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 means 'can'. 하 has no final consonant, so it takes -ㄹ: 할 수 있어요.

ko_meaning_en: The year we are in now

example.en: This year I'm going to study Korean hard.

form.q_en: Pick the form that makes a future plan.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 talks about plans and the future. After 하 it is 할 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: The year just before this year

example.ko: 작년에 제주도에 가서 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
example.roman: Jangnyeone jejudoe gaseo sajineul mani jjigeosseoyo.
example.en: Last year I went to Jeju Island and took a lot of photos.

form.q_en: Pick the verb form for something that happened last year.
form.why: 작년 (last year) is in the past, so the last verb takes -었어요. The tense goes only on the last verb, not on 가서.

ko_meaning_en: The year right after this year

example.en: I plan to enter university next year.

form.q_en: Pick the form for a plan ('plan to').
form.why: -(으)려고 하다 means 'plan to / intend to'. -(으)러 needs 가다/오다 after it, not 하다.

ko_meaning: 어떤 것 바로 뒤에 오는 것
ko_meaning_en: The thing that comes right after something

example.en: We have to get off at the next station.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'have to'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'have to'. 내리 + 어야 shortens to 내려야: 내려야 해요.

ko_meaning_en: The week just before this week

example.en: I was busy last week, so I couldn't exercise.

tokens.note: 에 marks time, 는 the topic

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 바쁘다 (to be busy).
form.why: When a stem ends in ㅡ, the ㅡ drops. The vowel before it (ㅏ in 바) picks -아서: 바빠서.

ko_meaning_en: The time from midnight until 12 noon

example.en: I'm busy in the morning because I have classes.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that gives the reason.
form.why: -어서 gives a reason: 수업이 있어서 바빠요. -지만 means 'but', and -러/-려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning_en: The time from 12 noon until the sun sets

example.ko: 오후 세 시에 친구를 만날 거예요.
example.roman: Ohu se sie chingureul mannal geoyeyo.
example.en: I'm going to meet a friend at three in the afternoon.

form.q_en: Pick the native number for 'three' before 시 (o'clock).
form.why: Hours use native numbers, and 셋 shortens to 세 before a counter: 세 시.

ko_meaning_en: The early morning before the sun rises

example.en: I got up at dawn and went to the mountain.

form.q_en: Pick the connector for 'got up and then (went)'.
form.why: -아서 links two actions in order. 나 + 아서 shortens to 나서, and the past tense goes only on the last verb.

ko_meaning: 하나를 똑같이 둘로 나눈 것 중 하나
ko_meaning_en: One of two equal parts of something

example.en: I get up at half past seven in the morning.

form.q_en: Pick the native number for 'seven' o'clock.
form.why: Hours use native numbers: 일곱 시. Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers, and 반 (half) replaces 삼십 분.

ko_meaning_en: The time from morning to night; 24 hours

example.en: I'm so busy that the day feels too short.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 짧다 (to be short).
form.why: 짧 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 짧아요. The double consonant ㄹㅂ stays in writing.

ko_meaning_en: The day, shown as a month and a day

example.en: I won't forget the exam date.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle that fits after a vowel.
form.why: 날짜 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를 (을 is for consonants).

ko_meaning_en: A chart that shows the dates and the days of the week

example.en: Looking at the calendar, tomorrow is a holiday.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'when I looked (I found that)'.
form.why: -(으)니까 can show what you found out by doing something: 보니까 = when I looked. -러 and -려고 show purpose.

ko_meaning: 지금의 차례, 또는 곧 오는 차례
ko_meaning_en: The current turn, or the one coming soon

example.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'this (coming)' weekend.
form.why: 이번 means 'this (current or coming)'. 지난 means 'last', which does not fit the future -(으)ㄹ 거예요; 작년 and 올해 are years.

ko_meaning_en: A day you rest from work or school

example.en: Banks don't open on holidays.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 않아요.
form.why: -지 않다 attaches to the verb stem: 열다 → 열지 않아요. The ㄹ stays before -지.

ko_meaning: 여름이나 겨울에 학교 수업을 쉬는 때
ko_meaning_en: A time in summer or winter when school classes stop

example.ko: 방학이 되면 할머니 집에 갈 거예요.
example.roman: Banghagi doemyeon halmeoni jibe gal geoyeyo.
example.en: When vacation starts, I'll go to my grandma's house.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'when / if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'when/if': 방학이 되면 = when vacation comes.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting people

example.en: Three customers came to the restaurant.

form.q_en: Pick 'two' before the counter 명.
form.why: People are counted with native numbers, and 둘 becomes 두 before a counter: 두 명.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting animals

example.en: I saw three rabbits at the park.

form.q_en: Pick the counter for animals.
form.why: 마리 counts animals. 명 is for people, 권 for books, and 병 for bottles.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting books or notebooks

example.en: I borrowed three books from the library.

form.q_en: Pick 'four' before the counter 권.
form.why: Books are counted with native numbers, and 넷 shortens to 네 before a counter: 네 권.

ko_meaning: 종이나 표처럼 얇은 것을 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting thin things like paper or tickets

example.ko: 친구하고 보려고 표를 두 장 샀어요.
example.roman: Chinguhago boryeogo pyoreul du jang sasseoyo.
example.en: I bought two tickets to watch it with my friend.

form.q_en: Pick 'one' before the counter 장.
form.why: 하나 becomes 한 before a counter: 한 장 = one sheet/ticket.

ko_meaning: 병에 든 물이나 주스를 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting water or juice in bottles

example.ko: 편의점에서 물 한 병을 사서 마셨어요.
example.roman: Pyeonuijeomeseo mul han byeongeul saseo masyeosseoyo.
example.en: I bought a bottle of water at the convenience store and drank it.

form.q_en: Pick the connector 'bought and then (drank it)'.
form.why: -아서 links two actions where the first leads to the second. The past tense is only on 마셨어요.

ko_meaning: 컵에 든 커피나 물을 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting coffee or water in cups

example.en: I drink two cups of coffee every morning.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'every'.
form.why: 마다 means 'every': 아침마다 = every morning.

ko_meaning_en: A word for counting age

example.en: My younger sibling is ten this year.

form.q_en: Pick 'ten' for an age with 살.
form.why: Age with 살 uses native numbers: 열 살. Sino-Korean 십 is not used with 살.

ko_meaning: 같은 일을 하는 횟수를 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting how many times you do something

example.ko: 일주일에 두 번 수영을 하러 가요.
example.roman: Iljuire du beon suyeongeul hareo gayo.
example.en: I go swimming twice a week.

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'go to (swim)'.
form.why: -(으)러 + 가다/오다 means 'go/come to do something': 수영을 하러 가요.

ko_meaning_en: A part of a building at the same height, like the 1st or 2nd floor

example.en: Take the elevator and go up to the seventh floor.

form.q_en: Pick the number used for floor names.
form.why: Floor names use Sino-Korean numbers: 칠 층 = the 7th floor. Native 일곱 is not used for floor names.

ko_meaning: 차나 컴퓨터 같은 기계를 세는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for counting machines like cars or computers

example.ko: 그 가게에서 자전거를 한 대 샀어요.
example.roman: Geu gageeseo jajeongeoreul han dae sasseoyo.
example.en: I bought a bicycle at that store.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you bought it.
form.ko: 그 가게___ 자전거를 한 대 샀어요.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (buying) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: Going to stores and buying things

example.en: I'm going to go shopping with my older sister on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 가다.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 is for plans. 가 has no final consonant, so it is 갈 거예요.

ko_meaning: 여러 가지 물건을 파는 아주 큰 가게
ko_meaning_en: A very big store that sells many kinds of things

example.en: The department store is expensive, so let's go to the market.

form.q_en: Pick the reason form that can come before a request.
form.why: Before a request or suggestion such as 가세요, a reason takes -(으)니까, not -아서/어서.

ko_meaning: 음식이나 생활에 필요한 물건을 파는 큰 가게
ko_meaning_en: A big store that sells food and everyday things

example.en: I went to the supermarket to buy eggs.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place you go to.
form.why: 에 marks the place you go to with 가다/오다.

ko_meaning_en: A small store that is open even at night

example.en: It's convenient because there's a convenience store near my house.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 있다.
form.why: 있 has the vowel ㅣ, so it takes -어서: 있어서 = because there is.

ko_meaning: 물건 값을 내다, 또는 숫자를 더하고 빼다
ko_meaning_en: To pay for things, or to add and subtract numbers

example.en: Can I pay by card?

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'by (means of)'.
form.why: (으)로 means 'by/with (a tool or method)'. After a vowel like 카드 it is 로.

ko_meaning_en: How big or small something is

example.en: These shoes are not the right size.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that makes the long negative.
form.why: The long negative is -지 않다: 맞지 않아요 = doesn't fit. 안 해요, 없어요 and 아니에요 cannot follow -지 here.

ko_meaning_en: The money you pay to buy something

example.en: It was cheap, so I bought two.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 싸다 (to be cheap).
form.why: 싸 + 아서 shortens to 싸서 (because it's cheap). The past tense does not go on -아서.

ko_meaning: 돈 대신에 물건 값을 낼 때 쓰는 작은 것
ko_meaning_en: A small thing used instead of money to pay

example.ko: 지갑에 카드가 없어서 계산을 못 했어요.
example.roman: Jigabe kadeuga eopseoseo gyesaneul mot haesseoyo.
example.en: There was no card in my wallet, so I couldn't pay.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that gives the reason.
form.why: -어서 gives the reason: 카드가 없어서 = because there was no card. -(으)면 cannot be used with a past result.

ko_meaning: 카드가 아닌 진짜 돈, 종이돈이나 동전
ko_meaning_en: Real money, not a card: bills or coins

example.en: You have to pay cash at the market.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle that fits after a consonant.
form.why: 현금 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을 (를 is for vowels).

ko_meaning: 돈을 낸 것을 보여 주는 종이
ko_meaning_en: A piece of paper that shows you paid

example.en: If you don't have the receipt, you can't get a refund.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'if': 영수증이 없으면 = if you don't have the receipt.

ko_meaning_en: To pick one out of several

example.en: I chose this bag.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 고르다.
form.why: 고르다 is 르-irregular: 르 drops and an extra ㄹ is added, so 고르 + 았어요 → 골랐어요.

ko_meaning: 가지고 있던 것을 다른 것으로 하다
ko_meaning_en: To replace something you have with something else

example.ko: 셔츠를 다른 색깔로 바꿀 수 있어요?
example.roman: Syeocheureul dareun saekkallo bakkul su isseoyo?
example.en: Can I exchange the shirt for a different color?

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'into / for (another one)'.
form.ko: 셔츠를 다른 색깔___ 바꿀 수 있어요?
form.why: (으)로 marks what something changes into. 색깔 ends in ㄹ, and after ㄹ you use 로, not 으로.

ko_meaning: 산 물건을 돌려주고 돈을 다시 받다
ko_meaning_en: To return something you bought and get your money back

example.en: The clothes were too small, so I got a refund.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 작다.
form.why: 작 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 작아서 = because they were small.

ko_meaning_en: To make the price of something cheaper

example.en: You can bargain at the market.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 수 있어요.
form.why: 깎 ends in a consonant, so it takes -을 수 있다: 깎을 수 있어요 = can bargain.

ko_meaning: 선물을 종이로 싸거나 음식을 가져갈 수 있게 담다
ko_meaning_en: To wrap a gift in paper, or to pack food so you can take it away

example.ko: 이 떡은 포장해서 가지고 갈 거예요.
example.roman: I tteogeun pojanghaeseo gajigo gal geoyeyo.
example.en: I'll have this rice cake packed and take it with me.

form.q_en: Pick the connector 'pack it and then (take it)'.
form.why: -아서/어서 links two steps: pack it, then take it. 하다 + -여서 → 해서, and it never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 여자가 허리 아래에 입는, 바지가 아닌 옷
ko_meaning_en: Clothing a woman wears below the waist that is not pants

example.en: I'm going to wear a short skirt today.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 짧다 before a noun.
form.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before a noun: 짧다 → 짧은 치마.

ko_meaning: 몸 위쪽에 입는, 단추가 있는 옷
ko_meaning_en: A top with buttons that you wear on your upper body

example.en: My shirt is dirty, so I have to do laundry.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 더럽다 (to be dirty).
form.why: 더럽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 더럽 + 어서 → 더러워서.

ko_meaning_en: Thin clothing you wear on your feet

example.en: It was cold, so I wore thick socks.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 두껍다 (thick) before a noun.
form.why: 두껍다 is ㅂ-irregular: before a noun the ㅂ becomes 우, so 두껍 + 은 → 두꺼운.

ko_meaning: 눈이 잘 보이게 눈 앞에 쓰는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Something you wear in front of your eyes to see well

example.en: I lost my glasses, so I bought new ones.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that gives the reason.
form.why: -어서 gives the reason: 잃어버려서 = because I lost them. 리 + 어서 shortens to 려서.

ko_meaning_en: What you wear on your hands when it is cold

example.en: It's cold, so wear gloves.

form.q_en: Pick the reason form that can come before a request (-세요).
form.why: Before a request like 끼세요, use -(으)니까 for the reason. 춥다 is ㅂ-irregular: 춥 + 으니까 → 추우니까.

ko_meaning_en: To put your feet into shoes or socks

example.en: We don't wear shoes inside the house.

tokens.note: 에서 marks the place of an action

form.q_en: Pick the verb used for wearing shoes.
form.why: 신다 is for shoes and socks. 입다 is for clothes, 쓰다 for hats, and 끼다 for gloves or glasses.

ko_meaning: 장갑이나 반지, 안경 같은 것을 몸에 하다
ko_meaning_en: To put on things like gloves, rings or glasses

example.en: Today I wore my glasses to school.

tokens.note: -고 = and; with wearing verbs it shows the state

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'put on and (went)'.
form.why: -고 links actions: put on glasses and went. With wearing verbs, -고 also means 'wearing'.

ko_meaning_en: To remove what you are wearing

example.en: You have to take off your shoes here.

form.q_en: Pick the correct '-아야/어야' form of 벗다.
form.why: 벗 has the vowel ㅓ, so it takes -어야: 벗어야 해요 = have to take off.

en: to tie; to wear (a tie, seat belt)
ko_meaning: 끈이나 넥타이 같은 것을 풀어지지 않게 묶다
ko_meaning_en: To tie something like a string or a tie so it doesn't come loose

example.en: When you get in a car, you have to wear your seat belt.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'when / if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'when/if': 차에 타면 = when you get in the car.

en: to suit; to go well with
ko_meaning_en: To look good together because they match well

example.ko: 이 모자는 아빠한테 잘 어울릴 거예요.
example.roman: I mojaneun appahante jal eoullil geoyeyo.
example.en: This hat will suit Dad well.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 거예요.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 makes a guess about the future: 어울릴 거예요 = will suit.

ko_meaning_en: Things like red and blue

example.en: I bought this umbrella because its color is pretty.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 예쁘다.
form.why: The ㅡ in 예쁘 drops before -어서: 예쁘 + 어서 → 예뻐서.

ko_meaning_en: The color of leaves and grass

example.en: In spring the mountains turn green.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'into (a color)'.
form.why: 초록색 ends in a consonant (not ㄹ), so it takes 으로. (으)로 shows what something changes into.

ko_meaning_en: A color like soil or coffee

example.ko: 갈색 신발은 이 바지와 어울리지 않아요.
example.roman: Galsaek sinbareun i bajiwa eoulliji anayo.
example.en: Brown shoes don't go with these pants.

form.q_en: Pick the particle 'with' that fits after a vowel.
form.ko: 갈색 신발은 이 바지___ 어울리지 않아요.
form.why: 와 is used after a vowel (바지); 과 after a consonant. 어울리다 takes 와/과 for 'go with'.

ko_meaning_en: A color made by mixing white and black

example.en: The sky is gray, so take an umbrella.

form.q_en: Pick the reason form that fits before a request (-세요).
form.why: Before a request like 가세요, a reason takes -(으)니까. -아서/어서 (including 이라서/이어서) cannot come before a request.

ko_meaning_en: Red mixed with white

example.ko: 분홍색 셔츠를 입은 사람이 제 남편이에요.
example.roman: Bunhongsaek syeocheureul ibeun sarami je nampyeonieyo.
example.en: The person wearing the pink shirt is my husband.

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 입다 ('who is wearing').
form.why: -(으)ㄴ after a verb makes a modifier: 셔츠를 입은 사람 = the person wearing (having put on) the shirt.

ko_meaning: 두 바퀴를 발로 돌려서 타는 것
ko_meaning_en: Something you ride by turning two wheels with your feet

example.en: I can't ride a bicycle.

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'can't ride'.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 means 'cannot'. 타 has no final consonant, so it is 탈 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: A long vehicle that runs on rails

example.en: It's faster if you go by train.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'by (a means of transport)'.
form.why: (으)로 marks the means of transport. 기차 ends in a vowel, so it takes 로.

ko_meaning: 바퀴가 두 개 있고 엔진으로 가는 차
ko_meaning_en: A vehicle with two wheels that runs on an engine

example.en: Motorcycles are dangerous, so ride slowly.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for a polite request ('please ride').
form.why: -(으)세요 makes a polite request: 천천히 타세요 = please ride slowly. The other endings cannot end a sentence.

ko_meaning: 버스가 서서 사람이 타고 내리는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where buses stop and people get on and off

example.ko: 정류장에 사람이 많아서 버스를 못 탔어요.
example.roman: Jeongnyujange sarami manaseo beoseureul mot tasseoyo.
example.en: There were so many people at the bus stop that I couldn't get on the bus.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 많다.
form.why: 많 has the vowel ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 많아서 = because there were many.

ko_meaning_en: A place where airplanes take off and land

example.ko: 내일 아침 일찍 공항에 가야 해요.
example.roman: Naeil achim iljjik gonghange gaya haeyo.
example.en: I have to go to the airport early tomorrow morning.

form.q_en: Pick the correct '-아야' form of 가다.
form.why: 가 + 아야 shortens to 가야: 가야 해요 = have to go.

ko_meaning: 버스나 지하철에서 내려서 다른 것을 타다
ko_meaning_en: To get off a bus or subway and take another one

example.en: I'll transfer to a bus at Seoul Station.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for what you transfer to.
form.why: (으)로 marks what you change to: 버스로 갈아타다 = transfer to a bus. 버스 ends in a vowel, so 로.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 하는 데 시간이 들다
ko_meaning_en: For some time to be needed to do something

example.en: It takes an hour from my home to the office.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'to / as far as'.
form.why: 에서 ... 까지 means 'from ... to': 집에서 회사까지 = from home to the office.

ko_meaning_en: To set off in order to go somewhere

example.en: If we leave now, we won't be late.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that makes a guess ('won't be late, I think').
form.why: -겠- expresses a guess about what will happen: 늦지 않겠어요. The past tense does not fit after an 'if' about now.

ko_meaning_en: To reach the place you were going to

example.en: I arrived at the airport and took a taxi.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place you arrive at.
form.why: 도착하다 takes 에 for the place you arrive at. 에서 would mean 'from' or the place of an activity.

ko_meaning_en: To make a car move and go

example.en: I drank alcohol, so I can't drive.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 마시다.
form.why: 마시 + 어서 shortens to 마셔서 (because I drank). -아서/어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 보통 사람들이 숟가락을 드는 손이 있는 쪽
ko_meaning_en: The side of the hand most people hold a spoon with

example.en: If you go right at the intersection, there's a post office.

form.q_en: Pick the particle that shows direction.
form.why: (으)로 shows direction. 오른쪽 ends in a consonant (not ㄹ), so it is 으로.

ko_meaning_en: The side opposite the right

example.ko: 왼쪽 다리를 다쳐서 걸을 수 없어요.
example.roman: Oenjjok darireul dachyeoseo georeul su eopseoyo.
example.en: I hurt my left leg, so I can't walk.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 걷다 before 수 없어요.
form.why: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so 걷 + 을 → 걸을 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: Straight forward without turning to the side

example.en: Cross the road and go straight.

form.q_en: Pick the connector 'cross and then (go)'.
form.why: -아서/어서 links two steps in order: cross, then go straight. It never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: To go from one side of a road or river to the other

example.ko: 아이는 혼자 길을 건널 수 없어요.
example.roman: Aineun honja gireul geonneol su eopseoyo.
example.en: The child can't cross the road alone.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form before 수 없어요.
form.why: 건너 has no final consonant, so it takes -ㄹ 수 없다: 건널 수 없어요 = can't cross.

ko_meaning_en: To change direction and go another way

example.en: Turn left at the next intersection.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite request form of 돌다.
form.why: With ㄹ-stem verbs the ㄹ drops before -세요: 돌다 → 도세요.

ko_meaning_en: A place close to somewhere

example.en: There are many good restaurants near my office.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 맛있다 before a noun.
form.why: Words ending in 있다/없다 (맛있다, 재미있다) take -는 before a noun: 맛있는 식당.

ko_meaning_en: A place where the road splits in four directions

example.en: This intersection is dangerous because there are many cars.

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle that fits after a vowel.
form.why: 는 marks the topic after a vowel (사거리); 은 is for consonants.

ko_meaning: 사람이 길을 건널 수 있게 하얀 줄을 그린 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place with white lines painted so people can cross the road

example.en: You have to cross carefully at crosswalks.

tokens.note: -아서/어서 can show the way you do something

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you do something.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where you do something (cross carefully), and 는 adds 'as for'.

ko_meaning: 빨간불, 초록불로 가고 서는 것을 알려 주는 등
ko_meaning_en: A light that tells you to go or stop with red and green

example.en: Cross when the traffic light turns green.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'when / if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'when/if': 바뀌면 건너세요 = cross when it changes.

ko_meaning_en: A structure built for people to live or work in

example.en: That tall building is our company.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 높다 before a noun.
form.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before a noun: 높다 → 높은 건물.

ko_meaning_en: A place where you send letters or packages

example.en: I went to the post office to send a letter home.

form.q_en: Pick the purpose form before 가다 ('to send').
form.why: -(으)러 + 가다 means 'go to do': 보내러 갔어요 = went to send.

ko_meaning_en: A place that sells medicine

example.en: I have a headache, so I'm going to go to the pharmacy.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 아프다.
form.why: The ㅡ of 아프 drops, and the vowel before it (ㅏ) picks -아서: 아파서.

ko_meaning_en: A shop that sells books

example.ko: 서점에서 한국어 책을 사고 커피를 마셨어요.
example.roman: Seojeomeseo hangugeo chaegeul sago keopireul masyeosseoyo.
example.en: I bought a Korean book at the bookstore and had coffee.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'and (then)'.
form.why: -고 lists actions one after another: 책을 사고 커피를 마셨어요.

ko_meaning_en: A shop where you drink coffee or tea

example.en: I want to read a book at a quiet cafe.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where an action happens.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (reading) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning: 머리를 자르거나 예쁘게 해 주는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where they cut or style your hair

example.en: I'm going to go to the hair salon to get a haircut.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 자르다 (to cut).
form.why: 자르다 is 르-irregular: 자르 + 았어요 → 잘랐어요. (자랐어요 comes from 자라다, 'to grow'.)

ko_meaning_en: A place where you watch movies or plays

example.ko: 극장이 너무 멀어서 집에서 영화를 봤어요.
example.roman: Geukjangi neomu meoreoseo jibeseo yeonghwareul bwasseoyo.
example.en: The theater was too far, so I watched a movie at home.

form.q_en: Pick the correct reason form of 멀다 (to be far).
form.why: 멀 has the vowel ㅓ, so it takes -어서: 멀어서. The ㄹ stays before 어.

ko_meaning: 옛날 물건이나 귀한 물건을 모아 보여 주는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place that collects and shows old or valuable objects

example.en: You must not take photos in the museum.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'if you take (photos)'.
form.why: 찍 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으면: 찍으면 안 돼요 = you must not take (photos).

ko_meaning_en: A place where police officers work

example.en: If you go to the police station, they will help you.

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 도와주다 (to help).
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 makes a future guess: 도와줄 거예요 = (they) will help.

ko_meaning: 여행하는 사람이 돈을 내고 자는 큰 건물
ko_meaning_en: A big building where travelers pay to sleep

example.en: This hotel is clean, but it's too expensive.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'but'.
form.why: -지만 means 'but' and links two contrasting facts. -(으)러/-(으)려고 express purpose, and 깨끗한 must come before a noun.

ko_meaning: 다른 나라에서 자기 나라의 일을 하는 곳
ko_meaning_en: An office in another country that does work for its own country

example.en: I have to go to the embassy to get a visa.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'have to (go)'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'have to': 가 + 아야 → 가야 해요.
